title: Compound Angle Identities & Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions (AA HL)

sections.heading: Compound angle formula for cosine

questions.q: Use the compound angle formula $\cos(A+B)=\cos A\cos B-\sin A\sin B$ to find the exact value of $\cos75^\circ$, writing $75^\circ=45^\circ+30^\circ$.
questions.answer: $\cos75^\circ=\cos45^\circ\cos30^\circ-\sin45^\circ\sin30^\circ$. Since $\cos45^\circ=\sin45^\circ=\sqrt{2}/2$, $\cos30^\circ=\sqrt{3}/2$, and $\sin30^\circ=1/2$, this gives $\cos75^\circ=(\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{2})/4$.

sections.heading: Compound angle formula for sine

questions.q: Use the compound angle formula $\sin(A-B)=\sin A\cos B-\cos A\sin B$ to find the exact value of $\sin15^\circ$, writing $15^\circ=45^\circ-30^\circ$.
questions.answer: $\sin15^\circ=\sin45^\circ\cos30^\circ-\cos45^\circ\sin30^\circ$. Since $\sin45^\circ=\cos45^\circ=\sqrt{2}/2$, $\cos30^\circ=\sqrt{3}/2$, and $\sin30^\circ=1/2$, this gives $\sin15^\circ=(\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{2})/4$. (This matches $\cos75^\circ$ above, as expected since $\sin15^\circ=\cos75^\circ$.)

sections.heading: Compound angle formula for tangent

questions.q: The compound angle formula for tangent is $\tan(A-B)=\dfrac{\tan A-\tan B}{1+\tan A\tan B}$. Use it with $A=45^\circ$ and $B=30^\circ$ to find the exact value of $\tan15^\circ$, giving your answer in simplified surd form.
questions.answer: Substituting $\tan45^\circ=1$ and $\tan30^\circ=1/\sqrt{3}$: $\tan15^\circ=(1-1/\sqrt{3})/(1+1/\sqrt{3})$. Multiplying top and bottom by $\sqrt{3}$: $\tan15^\circ=(\sqrt{3}-1)/(\sqrt{3}+1)$. Rationalising by multiplying top and bottom by $(\sqrt{3}-1)$: the numerator becomes $(\sqrt{3}-1)^2=4-2\sqrt{3}$ and the denominator becomes $(\sqrt{3}+1)(\sqrt{3}-1)=2$. So $\tan15^\circ=(4-2\sqrt{3})/2=2-\sqrt{3}$.

sections.heading: Proving identities using the compound angle formulas

questions.q: Prove that $\sin(A+B)+\sin(A-B)=2\sin A\cos B$.
questions.answer: Expand both: $\sin(A+B)=\sin A\cos B+\cos A\sin B$ and $\sin(A-B)=\sin A\cos B-\cos A\sin B$. Adding them, the $\cos A\sin B$ terms cancel: $\sin(A+B)+\sin(A-B)=2\sin A\cos B$, as required.

questions.q: Prove that $\cos(A+B)\cos(A-B)=\cos^2A-\sin^2B$.
questions.answer: Expand: $\cos(A+B)=\cos A\cos B-\sin A\sin B$ and $\cos(A-B)=\cos A\cos B+\sin A\sin B$. Their product is a difference of squares: $\cos^2A\cos^2B-\sin^2A\sin^2B$. Using $\cos^2B=1-\sin^2B$: this equals $\cos^2A(1-\sin^2B)-\sin^2A\sin^2B=\cos^2A-\sin^2B(\cos^2A+\sin^2A)=\cos^2A-\sin^2B$, as required.

sections.heading: Solving a trigonometric equation using a compound angle formula

questions.q: Solve $\sin(x+30^\circ)=\cos x$ for $0^\circ\leq x\leq360^\circ$.
questions.answer: Expand the left side first: $\sin(x+30^\circ)=\sin x\cos30^\circ+\cos x\sin30^\circ$, which is $(\sqrt{3}/2)\sin x+(1/2)\cos x$. Setting this equal to $\cos x$ and multiplying every term by 2: $\sqrt{3}\sin x+\cos x=2\cos x$. Rearranging: $\sqrt{3}\sin x=\cos x$, so $\tan x=1/\sqrt{3}$. Since this has period $180^\circ$: $x=30^\circ$ or $x=210^\circ$.

sections.heading: Evaluating reciprocal trigonometric functions from a given ratio

questions.q: Given $\cos\theta=\dfrac{3}{5}$ with $\theta$ in Quadrant I, find the exact values of $\sec\theta$, $\csc\theta$, and $\cot\theta$.
questions.answer: In Quadrant I all ratios are positive. By the Pythagorean identity, $\sin\theta=\sqrt{1-9/25}=4/5$. Then $\sec\theta=1/\cos\theta=5/3$, $\csc\theta=1/\sin\theta=5/4$, and $\cot\theta=\cos\theta/\sin\theta=3/4$.

sections.heading: Reciprocal trigonometric functions in another quadrant

questions.q: Given $\tan\theta=-2$ with $\theta$ in Quadrant II, find the exact values of $\sec\theta$, $\csc\theta$, and $\cot\theta$.
questions.answer: In Quadrant II, $\sin\theta>0$ and $\cos\theta<0$. Treating $\tan\theta=-2$ as opposite $=2$, adjacent $=-1$, the reference triangle has hypotenuse $\sqrt{5}$. So $\sin\theta=2/\sqrt{5}$ and $\cos\theta=-1/\sqrt{5}$. Then $\sec\theta=1/\cos\theta=-\sqrt{5}$, $\csc\theta=1/\sin\theta=\sqrt{5}/2$, and $\cot\theta=1/\tan\theta=-1/2$.

sections.heading: Deriving 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ

questions.q: Starting from the Pythagorean identity $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1$, divide through by $\cos^2\theta$ to derive $1+\tan^2\theta=\sec^2\theta$.
questions.answer: Dividing every term by $\cos^2\theta$: $\dfrac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta}+\dfrac{\cos^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta}=\dfrac{1}{\cos^2\theta}$, which is exactly $\tan^2\theta+1=\sec^2\theta$.

sections.heading: Deriving 1 + cot²θ = csc²θ

questions.q: Starting from the Pythagorean identity $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1$, divide through by $\sin^2\theta$ to derive $1+\cot^2\theta=\csc^2\theta$.
questions.answer: Dividing every term by $\sin^2\theta$: $\dfrac{\sin^2\theta}{\sin^2\theta}+\dfrac{\cos^2\theta}{\sin^2\theta}=\dfrac{1}{\sin^2\theta}$, which is exactly $1+\cot^2\theta=\csc^2\theta$.

sections.heading: Simplifying an expression using reciprocal identities

questions.q: Simplify $\sec\theta-\cos\theta$, expressing your answer in terms of $\sin\theta$ and $\tan\theta$.
questions.answer: $\sec\theta-\cos\theta=\dfrac{1}{\cos\theta}-\cos\theta=\dfrac{1-\cos^2\theta}{\cos\theta}=\dfrac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos\theta}=\sin\theta\cdot\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}=\sin\theta\tan\theta$.

sections.heading: Mixed application: combining reciprocal identities across quadrants

questions.q: Given $\sec\theta=13/5$ with $\theta$ in Quadrant IV, find the exact value of $\sin\theta+\cot\theta$.
questions.answer: $\cos\theta=5/13$. By the Pythagorean identity, $\sin^2\theta=1-25/169=144/169$. Since $\theta$ is in Quadrant IV, $\sin\theta=-12/13$. Then $\cot\theta=\cos\theta/\sin\theta=(5/13)/(-12/13)=-5/12$. Adding a common denominator of 156: $\sin\theta+\cot\theta=-144/156-65/156=-209/156$.

sections.heading: Compound angle formula for sine (sum form)

questions.q: Use the compound angle formula $\sin(A+B)=\sin A\cos B+\cos A\sin B$ to find the exact value of $\sin75^\circ$, writing $75^\circ=45^\circ+30^\circ$.
questions.answer: $\sin75^\circ=\sin45^\circ\cos30^\circ+\cos45^\circ\sin30^\circ$. Since $\sin45^\circ=\cos45^\circ=\sqrt{2}/2$, $\cos30^\circ=\sqrt{3}/2$, and $\sin30^\circ=1/2$, this gives $\sin75^\circ=(\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{2})/4$.

sections.heading: Compound angle formula for tangent (sum form)

questions.q: Use $\tan(A+B)=\dfrac{\tan A+\tan B}{1-\tan A\tan B}$ with $A=45^\circ$ and $B=30^\circ$ to find the exact value of $\tan75^\circ$, giving your answer in simplified surd form.
questions.answer: Substituting $\tan45^\circ=1$ and $\tan30^\circ=1/\sqrt{3}$: $\tan75^\circ=(1+1/\sqrt{3})/(1-1/\sqrt{3})$. Multiplying top and bottom by $\sqrt{3}$: $\tan75^\circ=(\sqrt{3}+1)/(\sqrt{3}-1)$. Rationalising by multiplying top and bottom by $(\sqrt{3}+1)$: the numerator becomes $(\sqrt{3}+1)^2=4+2\sqrt{3}$ and the denominator becomes $(\sqrt{3}-1)(\sqrt{3}+1)=2$. So $\tan75^\circ=(4+2\sqrt{3})/2=2+\sqrt{3}$.

sections.heading: Finding an exact value in Quadrant II

questions.q: Use the compound angle formula $\cos(A+B)=\cos A\cos B-\sin A\sin B$ to find the exact value of $\cos105^\circ$, writing $105^\circ=60^\circ+45^\circ$.
questions.answer: $\cos105^\circ=\cos60^\circ\cos45^\circ-\sin60^\circ\sin45^\circ$. Since $\cos60^\circ=1/2$, $\cos45^\circ=\sin45^\circ=\sqrt{2}/2$, and $\sin60^\circ=\sqrt{3}/2$, this gives $\cos105^\circ=(\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{6})/4$ — negative, as expected since $105^\circ$ is in Quadrant II.

sections.heading: Deriving the double-angle formula from the compound angle formula

questions.q: By setting $A=B=\theta$ in $\sin(A+B)=\sin A\cos B+\cos A\sin B$, derive the double-angle formula $\sin2\theta=2\sin\theta\cos\theta$.
questions.answer: Setting $A=B=\theta$: $\sin(\theta+\theta)=\sin\theta\cos\theta+\cos\theta\sin\theta$. The right side has two identical terms, so $\sin2\theta=2\sin\theta\cos\theta$, as required.

sections.heading: A second identity from the compound angle formulas

questions.q: Prove that $\cos(A-B)-\cos(A+B)=2\sin A\sin B$.
questions.answer: Expand both: $\cos(A-B)=\cos A\cos B+\sin A\sin B$ and $\cos(A+B)=\cos A\cos B-\sin A\sin B$. Subtracting, the $\cos A\cos B$ terms cancel: $\cos(A-B)-\cos(A+B)=2\sin A\sin B$, as required.

sections.heading: Solving another trigonometric equation using a compound angle formula

questions.q: Solve $\sin(x+60^\circ)=\cos x$ for $0^\circ\leq x\leq360^\circ$.
questions.answer: Expand the left side: $\sin(x+60^\circ)=\sin x\cos60^\circ+\cos x\sin60^\circ$, which is $(1/2)\sin x+(\sqrt{3}/2)\cos x$. Setting this equal to $\cos x$ and multiplying every term by 2: $\sin x+\sqrt{3}\cos x=2\cos x$. Rearranging: $\sin x=(2-\sqrt{3})\cos x$, so $\tan x=2-\sqrt{3}$, which (as found earlier in this worksheet) equals $\tan15^\circ$. Since this has period $180^\circ$: $x=15^\circ$ or $x=195^\circ$.

sections.heading: A quick simplification from the Pythagorean identity

questions.q: Simplify $(\sec\theta+\tan\theta)(\sec\theta-\tan\theta)$.
questions.answer: This is a difference of squares: $\sec^2\theta-\tan^2\theta$. By the identity $1+\tan^2\theta=\sec^2\theta$, this equals $1$.

sections.heading: Reciprocal trigonometric functions in Quadrant III

questions.q: Given $\sec\theta=-13/12$ with $\theta$ in Quadrant III, find the exact values of $\sin\theta$, $\cos\theta$, and $\tan\theta$.
questions.answer: $\cos\theta=1/\sec\theta=-12/13$. In Quadrant III, $\sin\theta$ is also negative. By the Pythagorean identity, $\sin^2\theta=1-144/169=25/169$, so $\sin\theta=-5/13$. Then $\tan\theta=\sin\theta/\cos\theta=(-5/13)/(-12/13)=5/12$.

sections.heading: Connecting a co-function identity to the reciprocal functions

questions.q: Using the compound angle formula for cosine, show that $\cos(90^\circ-\theta)=\sin\theta$, and hence prove that $\sec(90^\circ-\theta)=\csc\theta$.
questions.answer: $\cos(90^\circ-\theta)=\cos90^\circ\cos\theta+\sin90^\circ\sin\theta=0+\sin\theta=\sin\theta$. Then $\sec(90^\circ-\theta)=1/\cos(90^\circ-\theta)=1/\sin\theta=\csc\theta$, as required.

sections.heading: Solving an equation involving a reciprocal function

questions.q: Solve $\csc\theta=2$ for $0^\circ\leq\theta\leq360^\circ$.
questions.answer: $\csc\theta=2\Rightarrow\sin\theta=1/2$. Since sine is positive in Quadrants I and II: $\theta=30^\circ$ or $\theta=150^\circ$.

sections.heading: Proving a reciprocal identity from scratch

questions.q: Prove that $\tan\theta+\cot\theta=\sec\theta\csc\theta$.
questions.answer: $\tan\theta+\cot\theta=\sin\theta/\cos\theta+\cos\theta/\sin\theta$. Combining over a common denominator, this is $(\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta)/(\sin\theta\cos\theta)$. Since $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1$, this equals $1/(\sin\theta\cos\theta)$. On the other side, $\sec\theta\csc\theta=(1/\cos\theta)(1/\sin\theta)=1/(\sin\theta\cos\theta)$. The two sides match, as required.

sections.heading: A capstone exact-value application

questions.q: Find the exact value of $\cos15^\circ$ (writing $15^\circ=45^\circ-30^\circ$), then use it together with $\cos75^\circ=(\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{2})/4$ found earlier to compute $\cos75^\circ-\cos15^\circ$ exactly.
questions.answer: $\cos15^\circ=\cos45^\circ\cos30^\circ+\sin45^\circ\sin30^\circ$. This equals $(\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{6})/4$. Now subtract: $\cos75^\circ-\cos15^\circ=(\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{2})/4-(\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{2})/4$. The $\sqrt{6}$ terms cancel, leaving $-2\sqrt{2}/4$. This simplifies to $-\sqrt{2}/2$.
